literal: To a person who says 'I will raise my family', the deity, tucking up its garment, will itself go before.
translation: To the person who resolves, 'I will elevate my family,' the divine power will gird up its loins and lead the way.
modern: என் குடியை உயர்த்துவேன் என்று முயலும் ஒருவனுக்கு, தெய்வமே தன் ஆடையைக் கட்டிக்கொண்டு அவனுக்கு முன்னே வந்து உதவி செய்யும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of determination in uplifting one's family or community. When a person takes a firm resolve to work for the elevation of their clan, even the divine power is said to hasten to their aid. The poet uses the vivid image of the deity 'girding up its loins' (tucking up its garment) to show that active, enthusiastic assistance is guaranteed to those who take initiative. It beautifully illustrates that sincere human effort commands divine cooperation.
